decisions.reason: “Came cheap” preserves the sense that death had become commonplace and low-value.
“Made the impossible their new normal” keeps the meaning in natural English.
The shorter phrasing preserves the thought without changing its scope.
The separated “Please” preserves the plea while keeping the emphasis.
Korean says “at this very moment”; SOL drops the emphasis in 지금 이 순간.
The source says accepted common sense collapsed, not merely their idea of what was possible.
The sound effect is a roar; “Rooooom” changes the sound category.
The participial phrasing preserves the steel rain stopping without changing the action.
“Gripped them all” and “emerged” preserve the silence, shock, and reveal.
The pronoun keeps the demon accusation while avoiding an awkward repetition.
“Spat out” preserves the forceful delivery in 토해 냈다; “gave voice” softens it.
The concise phrasing keeps the Skeleton King’s smirk and gaze.
Korean says “let’s finish this”; “we should” weakens the direct suggestion.
“Wounds large and small” retains the source’s range in natural English.
“His injuries were the last thing on his mind” preserves his disregard for them.
“Anyone” preserves the incredulous question without changing its meaning.
The source explicitly says he muttered; SOL drops that speech action.
The phrasing clearly conveys that he sees the blood and corpses left by the whirlwind.
The reserve force and Amir’s status as commander and finest warrior remain intact.
“Had been with them” naturally conveys that Amir was among the force.
“Killed by one man” preserves the disbelief and the source’s meaning.
The repeated “impossible” retains both disbelief and incomprehension.
The revised phrasing preserves the trembling hand and groan.
The cut-off word still communicates the interrupted “impossible.”
The one-word reply preserves the Skeleton King’s abrupt interruption.
The sentence keeps the wavering voice abruptly cut off.
The guillotine image and even delivery are retained in natural phrasing.
Present-tense “can” suits the claim about Jin Taekyung’s ability.
The eyes-blazing description preserves the man’s anger.
The aura and killing intent still emanate from him and engulf the space.
The pressure conveys that an ordinary Hunter could barely breathe.
“More familiar than anything else” preserves the undead’s familiarity with killing intent.
The source says he was in contact with death; “stood close” weakens that image.
The man’s aura remains the comparison to the undead’s familiar energy.
“If I’m generous” naturally captures 잘 쳐줘야.
실소 conveys a snort or derisive chuckle; “quiet laugh” loses that attitude.
The split sentence removes repetition while retaining the contrast.
The source explicitly says he would have angered “that guy”; SOL replaces the pointed reference with “him.”
SOL drops the source’s repeated “God” and the description of God as great.
Korean says he looked around while echoing the words; SOL omits the echo.
“Corpses lay in every direction” preserves the scene without an unnecessary ground reference.
“Surely this isn’t” captures the source’s incredulous rhetorical question.
The conditional recast keeps the Skeleton King’s sardonic concession.
The line naturally specifies that the magically empowered voice reached both groups.
SOL already says the voice reached Hunters and fanatics, preserving the deleted sentence’s meaning.
The cold-water image and the Hunters taking up weapons again preserve the source’s effect.
The shift from one human to many follows the source’s deliberate correction.
“Since coming into the world” preserves the timeline and reads naturally.
“Kept dying” and “didn’t fight only” preserve the repeated deaths and contrast.
The source says they had values worth protecting; “things” makes that more generic.
The source says he could not accept that different kinds of death existed, not that they might exist.
“More closely than any other monster” preserves the comparison clearly.
“Stood beside them” preserves the Skeleton King’s companionship with humans.
“At last” preserves the realization and its timing.
The line preserves the realization that these deaths could not all simply be called deaths.
“Lovers” accurately renders 연인 and keeps the contrast with friends.
“Died away” preserves the image of lives fading after burning brightly.
“Went forward prepared to die” preserves the source’s resolve.
SOL drops the explicit image of fighting without retreat even in the face of death.
허상 is an illusion; “falsehood” changes the source’s image.
숨을 삼켰다 means he swallowed a breath; “caught his breath” changes the physical reaction.
“Wandering gaze” preserves the directionless, wavering look.
The fragment connects naturally to the resentment and confusion described immediately before it.
The source describes some followers; SOL’s “they” can imply all of them.
The source stumbles through three repetitions of “I”; SOL removes one.
The source says he wanted to shout at those people; SOL adds that their faith was wavering.
“Silver tongue” preserves the source’s image of a demon’s persuasive speech.
“Gone blank” naturally conveys the whitened mind, while retaining the repeated words.
The recast preserves the involuntary clenching, broken molar, and dreamlike distance.
The source says corpses filled every direction; SOL narrows this to the ground around him.
The singular pool matches the source’s 피 웅덩이.
The phrasing preserves the expected green, beautiful promised land.
“Almighty God” preserves the source’s description of an omnipotent God.
The recast preserves the question he swallowed rather than spoke.
“Dreamlike haze” and “brightened the darkness” preserve the vision and light.
The sentence retains the man’s forgetting who held the sword.
The sword, its chosen-only brilliance, and the man’s question to the demon remain clear.
The source says everything had stopped; “seemed to have stopped” adds uncertainty.
“Turned in the same direction” preserves the action without an unnecessary head detail.
The recast preserves that only Amir knew the name and the man could not know it.
“Telling yourselves” preserves their belief that everything was God’s will.
“Strode forward” naturally conveys his rough, forceful advance.
The pool still splashes in every direction, and the blood-covered young man ignores it.
The past-perfect tense fits the recollection of disasters that had already happened.
“Families had vanished” preserves the source’s image of families disappearing in the disasters.
“People had caused it” clearly preserves that the disasters were man-made.
The source calls a god who watches over them an idiot; SOL changes the insult to not being stupid enough.
씹어 뱉듯이 conveys spitting out each word; SOL drops that forceful delivery.
“Staggered in shock” preserves their unsteady reaction and the others’ belated realization.
The counterfactual retains the point that a few words could not have changed their hearts.
The source is a direct exclamation at the heretic; SOL adds “say such a thing.”
“Rushed him” makes the attack target clear from context without changing the action.
“Yeah” preserves 그래 and the blunt, approving reply.
The blades and bodies remain the objects pierced and sliced.
“Only then” preserves the timing of the survivors’ realization.
“Earlier whirlwind” preserves the reference without changing the event.
“Caught within its reach” preserves who was struck by the whirlwind.
The eerie noise still fills an area more than ten meters across.
The revised phrasing preserves the arrows and daggers reversing course and killing their owners.
The shorter phrasing retains the dying-gasp image.
“Beyond recognition” preserves that half the attackers were torn apart beyond identification.
The source’s image is body parts filling the empty places left by screams; SOL generalizes this to silence.
The line preserves Hamid’s wide-eyed stare and the sword hilt slipping from his hand.
The lowered sword and Magic Johnson standing in midair remain clear.
Korean says “at this very moment”; SOL’s “that moment” weakens the immediacy.
“Pass judgment or grant forgiveness” preserves both roles naturally.
The plea, trembling voice, and desperate need to survive remain intact.
“Let go of his sword” preserves the action before he kneels.
“Threw his faith into the trash” retains the shattered faith and trash image.
The unwavering look and sudden reach remain intact.
“Searing” preserves the heat’s intensity; SOL reduces it to ordinary heat.
온순하게 means quietly or gently; “without resistance” invents a physical reaction.
SOL’s exclamation mark adds emphasis not present in the source sound effect.
The recast makes clear that weapons fell and people knelt on the blood-soaked sand.
“Dim light of dawn” preserves 어스름한 새벽녘.
“Looking west” preserves the direction of Jin Taekyung’s gaze and the lingering darkness.
